[00:00:00.676] Hello, everyone, welcome back to this course on engineering chemistry. We will continue with module 6 on corrosion chemistry, and today's class we are going to talk about corrosion control. In that we will look at metallic coating and specifically galvanization and tinning.
[00:00:21.700] When we talk of corrosion control, the first thing which comes to our mind is to create a barrier between the surface and the environment. Now, except for the very noble metals, we know that all metals will undergo corrosion when exposed to the right kind of environment.
[00:00:39.748] So protective coating is a very good method by which we can control corrosion to a great extent. In protective coating, we have metallic coating, inorganic coating, and organic coating.
[00:00:53.220] Then another method of corrosion control is to use corrosion inhibitors. Again, we have two classes here: anodic inhibitors and catodic inhibitors.
[00:01:02.500] The other method would be cathodic protection, and in that we are going to study about two methods in there, that is sacrificial anode method and the impressed cathodic current method. Finally, we will study about anodic protection, which is also known as impressed anodic current method.
[00:01:21.508] Let us start with protective coatings. The first type of coating we are going to look at is metallic coating. So what would that be as the name suggests? Corrosion of the base metal can be prevented by coating it with a layer of another metal over it.
[00:01:40.420] Now, since we are coating one metal over another metal, this coating metal could be either anodic to the base metal or it could be cathodic to the base metal. Therefore, we will have two types of coatings which are possible.
[00:01:58.800] One is called anodic metal coating where we are going to coat a layer of metal which is anodic with respect to the base metal. A good example would be if you have an iron article and you are covering it with zinc metal, this would be
[00:02:16.096] anodic metal coating and then there is another method where we which we call it as the cathodic metal coating where we are going to coat the metal with um another metal
[00:02:28.624] Which is cathodic with respect to the base metal. And an example for that would be an iron article which is coated with tin.
[00:02:38.788] Let us talk about anonic metal coating. As I said just now, the coating metal is more active with respect to the base metal. So even if the base metal

[00:03:19.556] To the base metal. So the coating is anodic with respect to the base metal. Therefore, even if there is a gap here, we will find that if the coating is not completely covering the surface, there is a gap on the surface. You have studied that.
